neet_che_u06_t01_1.working: A liquid boils when its vapour pressure equals the external (atmospheric) pressure.

neet_che_u06_t01_2.working: Equilibrium vapour pressure depends only on temperature, not on volume or the amount of liquid. Liquid remains, so the pressure is restored to 3.17 kPa.

neet_che_u06_t01_3.working: Liquid water occupies less volume than ice. By Le Chatelier's principle, higher pressure favours the smaller volume, so some ice melts.

neet_che_u06_t01_4.working: A is melting/freezing (II). B is evaporation/condensation (I). C is sublimation equilibrium (IV). D is dissolution/crystallisation (III).

neet_che_u06_t01_5.working: A is true: vapour pressure is independent of the amount of liquid. B is true: water boils at 373 K at 1.013 bar. C is true as NCERT lists camphor and NH4Cl as subliming solids, though NH4Cl actually decomposes. D is false: at equilibrium the two rates are equal. E is false: vapour pressure depends only on temperature.
